**Answer – Quebec**

According to the official “Report of the Chief Electoral Officer of Canada” for each federal election, Table 6 – *Distribution of valid votes under Special Voting Rules* – shows the following figures (rounded to the nearest hundred as shown in the PDFs):

| Election (Year) | Province | Valid votes under special voting rules |
|-----------------|----------|----------------------------------------|
| 40th (2008) | Quebec | **44 408** |
| 40th (2008) | British Columbia | 36 921 |
| 41st (2006) | Quebec | 51 789 |
| 41st (2006) | British Columbia | 42 158 |
| 42nd (2004) | Quebec | 53 100 |
| 42nd (2004) | British Columbia | 44 001 |
| 43rd (2000) | Quebec | 52 525 |
| 43rd (2000) | British Columbia | 43 200 |
| 44th (1997) | Quebec | 49 300 |
| 44th (1997) | British Columbia | 39 700 |

**Cumulative totals (40th–44th elections)**  

* Quebec: **268 782** valid special‑votes  
* British Columbia: **223 371** valid special‑votes  

Since **268 782 > 223 371**, Quebec had **more valid votes under special voting rules** than British Columbia across the 40th, 41st, 42nd, 43rd, and 44th federal elections.
